foundations.title: 01 · Foundations, Linux & networking
foundations.intro: Start here. Understand processes, files, permissions, DNS, HTTP and the shell before adding cloud services.

git-and-code.title: 02 · Git, Python & automation
git-and-code.intro: Learn enough programming to build and diagnose systems. Start with one language and one version-control workflow.

cloud.title: 03 · Cloud: choose one provider
cloud.intro: Learn IAM, networking, compute, storage, databases, reliability and billing on one provider first. Reading is often free; accounts, labs and deployed resources may cost money.

containers.title: 04 · Containers & Kubernetes
containers.intro: Learn images and container networking first. Use a local cluster before paying for a managed Kubernetes service.

infrastructure-as-code.title: 05 · Infrastructure as code
infrastructure-as-code.intro: Make changes reviewable and reproducible. Treat state, credentials and teardown as part of the design.

delivery.title: 06 · CI/CD, GitOps & releases
delivery.intro: Build a small pipeline, deliberately break it, then add the checks that would have caught the failure.

observability-and-sre.title: 07 · Observability, SRE & incidents
observability-and-sre.intro: Measure user-visible behavior, investigate failures and practice recovery. Start with logs and a useful health check.

security-and-cost.title: 08 · Security, supply chain & cost
security-and-cost.intro: Practice least privilege, secret hygiene and cost awareness throughout the roadmap.

architecture.title: 09 · System design & data
architecture.intro: Understand caching, queues, databases and failure modes by following a request through a real system.

engineering-blogs.title: 10 · Engineering blogs worth reading
engineering-blogs.intro: The video names Netflix, Google and Cloudflare. The other publications below extend that reading list. Read one post actively and reproduce a small idea.

outage-stories.title: 11 · Outage stories & postmortems
outage-stories.intro: Start with the Cloudflare report shown in the video. These are historical case studies, not descriptions of the services’ current health.

papers.title: 12 · Papers: systems first, AI optional
papers.intro: Read for the problem, assumptions, mechanism, evidence and limits. The video mentions AI and transformers as examples; AI is an optional extension, not a cloud prerequisite.

open-source-and-people.title: 13 · Open source, people & practice collections
open-source-and-people.intro: Follow work and explanations, then read source code and contribute a scoped improvement. These links do not imply endorsement by the people or projects listed.

community-projects.title: 14 · Community projects from my stars
community-projects.intro: Selected implementation examples from aniketsingh1023’s public stars. Read the prerequisites, account-specific values, security choices and cleanup steps before using any example. These are learning references, not audited production templates.

ai-and-mlops.title: 15 · Optional AI & MLOps extension
ai-and-mlops.intro: The video mentions AI as a research-reading example. These starred resources are an optional extension after you can explain the underlying application, container, identity and delivery workflow. API usage, cloud deployment and compute may cost money.
